digest.component_or_area: LLM provider qualifier decision in config resolution
propositions: Provider qualification currently uses a shape regex (_PROVIDER_QUALIFIER_RE) to test if a colon-delimited prefix looks like a provider name, which rejects valid slash-containing names (gateway/openai) and accepts non-members (google_genai, test).
A typo'd configured provider (e.g., bedrok instead of bedrock) is accepted at config resolution and only fails later at provider construction, instead of raising immediately with a diagnostic.
Future model IDs with lowercase-dotless pre-colon prefixes risk being silently promoted to providers by the shape regex, repeating the assumptions that produced the Bedrock colon defect.
Provider qualification must migrate from shape-based testing to membership testing against a static frozenset of 24 known provider names derived from pydantic-ai's runtime registries.

Configured providers must be validated by membership and raise LLMConfigError before composition; unrecognized inline prefixes must remain unqualified without raising, to preserve colon-bearing model IDs like Bedrock's.
The static KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES set and runtime registries must be kept in sync via drift detection tests to prevent silent divergence when pydantic-ai adds providers.
